newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: New fighting erupts in southern Philippines.
newsitem.headline: New fighting erupts in southern Philippines.

text.p: More fighting erupted in the southern Philippines on Wednesday despite an order by President Fidel Ramos for the military to cease offensive activity to clear the way for ceasefire talks, an army spokesman said.

There were no immediate reports of casualties in the clashes, which broke out after about 100 guerrillas of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) shelled an army command outpost in Buldon town in Maguindanao province, spokesman Captain Salih Indanan told reporters.
Soldiers countered by bombarding suspected rebel positions with 105-mm howitzers, Indanan told reporters.
MILF vice chairman for political affairs Ghazali Jaafar accused the military of provoking the new round of fighting by opening fire on rebels returning to their main camp in Buldon.

Ramos on Tuesday ordered a halt to all army operations against rebels to allow for the resumption of ceasefire talks cancelled last month after a series of skirmishes between soldiers and the rebels in Maguindanao and North Cotabato.
The military had said it killed more than 70 rebels in the June fighting and 15 soldiers had died.
The MILF is fighting for an Islamic state on southern Mindanao island, which Moslems in this largely Christian country regard as their ancestral homeland.
Manila signed a peace deal last year with the mainstream Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF) but the MILF was not a party to the accord.
